drills.title: What does assigning through a reference actually do?
drills.promptMd: Trace each variable carefully after `ref = y` executes, then pick the output.
drills.explanationMd: `ref = y` never reseats the reference — references are permanently bound. It copies `y`'s value (2) into whatever `ref` currently refers to, which is `x`. So after the assignment `x == 2` and `y == 2`. Many learners expect `ref` to start aliasing `y`; that operation simply does not exist for references.

drills.title: Does `auto` preserve `const`?
drills.promptMd: Predict what prints — pay close attention to what `auto` deduces.
drills.explanationMd: `auto` deduces `y` as plain `int`, not `const int`. The `const` on `x` is *top-level const* — it qualifies the object itself — and `auto` drops top-level const because a copy is free to be mutable. `x` is never modified (it stays 42), but `y` is an independent, modifiable copy that becomes 99. If you wanted a const copy you'd write `const auto y { x };`.

drills.title: Fix the swap-by-pointer function
drills.promptMd: The function is supposed to swap the two ints the pointers point at, but it leaves them unchanged. Find the bug and fix it.
drills.explanationMd: The broken version swaps the *pointer variables themselves* (`a` and `b` are local copies of the pointers). Since pointers are passed by value, reseating `a` and `b` only changes the function's local copies — the caller's ints are never touched. The fix is to dereference before swapping: `*a` and `*b` are the actual integers in the caller's memory, and writing through them modifies the caller's data.

drills.title: Write `findFirst` using `std::optional`
drills.promptMd: Implement `findFirst` so it returns the index of the first occurrence of `target` in `text`, or `std::nullopt` if not found.
drills.explanationMd: Loop over each index, compare `text[i]` to `target`, and return the index wrapped in an `optional` as soon as you find a match. After the loop, if no match was found, return `std::nullopt`. The `static_cast<std::size_t>` is needed because `text.length()` returns an unsigned type — comparing it to a signed `int` loop counter without a cast triggers a signed/unsigned comparison warning.

drills.title: Write two in/out parameter functions
drills.promptMd: Implement `scale` and `clampToZero` — both take a non-const reference as an in/out parameter and modify the caller's variable directly.
drills.explanationMd: In both functions the reference parameter is an *in/out* parameter: the function both reads the caller's current value and writes back a new one through the same reference. `scale` reads `score`, multiplies it, and writes back through the same name — the caller's variable updates. `clampToZero` reads `score`, checks it against `threshold`, and conditionally writes zero back. Nothing is returned; the side-effect through the reference is the whole point.
